title: Compiler Diagnostics and Analyzers
keywords: reflection, attributes, expression trees, and compiler tools
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of compiler diagnostics and analyzers in a C#/.NET program.
Predict the result of the included C# example and verify the documented output.
Apply compiler diagnostics and analyzers to a small task and identify one relevant boundary, limitation, or version requirement.

content.intro: Compiler Diagnostics and Analyzers is lesson 169 in Reflection, Attributes, Expression Trees, and Compiler Tools. Exceptions represent failures that should interrupt the ordinary path; diagnostics should add actionable context without exposing secrets or hiding the root cause.
content.why_it_matters: Reflection and compiler tools are powerful but should be introduced after ordinary static code and types are familiar. This lesson focuses on compiler diagnostics and analyzers and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Exceptions represent failures that should interrupt the ordinary path; diagnostics should add actionable context without exposing secrets or hiding the root cause.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to learn it
content_blocks.text: Start with the smallest valid case for compiler diagnostics and analyzers. Predict the output, run or inspect the example in the stated toolchain, then change one input or rule and compare the result. For production code, record assumptions and verify boundary cases.

items.title: Compiler diagnostics
items.text: Separate source diagnostics, emitted assembly artifacts, and runtime execution; they are different stages with different failure modes.

items.title: Code analysis
items.text: For code analysis, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to compiler diagnostics and analyzers, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: Built-in .NET analyzers
items.text: Separate compile-time analysis from runtime inspection and document when reflection or generation changes normal assumptions.

items.title: Editor configuration
items.text: Keep environment-specific configuration outside source code. Read settings at a clear boundary, validate required values on startup, and never commit credentials or print them in diagnostics.

items.title: Writing or configuring analyzer rules
items.text: Confirm the SDK and compiler versions first, then use one small project to verify the toolchain.

items.title: Automating quality checks
items.text: For automating quality checks, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to compiler diagnostics and analyzers, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates compiler diagnostics and analyzers. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates compiler diagnostics and analyzers rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for compiler diagnostics and analyzers before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.
content.expected_output: Treat warnings as reviewable engineering feedback.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
